sign_convention: value_percent and quartiles_percent store positive percentage-improvement magnitudes; reported and spread_reported preserve source text verbatim. No GlassSkin-point outcomes are precomputed here.

comparisons.caveats: Weeks 4 and 8 use the FDA mean-change series; their U(...) parentheticals are untyped and cannot supply an SD or SE. Week 12 is a registry LS mean with a typed SD of percentage change. Ns are analysis-set Ns, not observed visit attendance. Same product and closely matched protocol as the fitted 301 trial, so this tests replication rather than cross-population generalisation.

Registry LS means and typed SDs describe percentage change; Ns are analysis-set Ns, not observed visit attendance. Same product and closely matched protocol as the fitted 301 trial, so this tests replication rather than cross-population generalisation.

This endpoint comes from a different study than the calibrated Shah et al. series, with an unnamed formulation and evaluator-blinded rather than open-label design. The observed baseline is unavailable, so a later comparison is interpretable only on the percentage scale and depends on an assumed evaluation baseline. The efficacy N is 162; the separate safety N must not be substituted.

comparisons.trial: Twelve-week, multicenter, placebo-controlled, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, comparative phase II/III study of benzoyl peroxide gel in patients with acne vulgaris: A secondary publication
comparisons.caveats: This is the same trial used in calibration. End of study means week 12 or early discontinuation, so there is no single observed day and these quartiles do not belong to the exact week-12 row. It is not independent validation. The IQR is a partial plausibility check on the borrowed response spread / sigma, not a typed SD of percentage change or a Tier 1 spread verdict.
